stories.title: Engineered molecular glue aims to stabilize aging eggs
stories.summary: Researchers are using engineered molecular glue to stabilize cohesin, a protein complex that holds chromosomes together. As this glue degrades with age, it causes genetic errors in eggs. The intervention aims to address the leading cause of age-related infertility and miscarriage in women over 40.

stories.title: New platform identifies metabolic targets in cancer
stories.summary: A new platform reveals how specific cancer-causing mutations rewire cell metabolism to fuel tumor growth. The study highlights that tumors possess distinct metabolic needs even when located within the same organ, offering potential new targets for treatment. Cancer cells remain hungry, regardless of the specific menu.

stories.title: An engineered 'glue' for aged eggs could prevent premature chromosome separation
DNA duplication study highlights cancer vulnerability
stories.summary: Researchers at CNIO and Stanford University have identified a new mechanism involved in how cells duplicate DNA during division. By studying how cells tolerate damage during this process, the team hopes to uncover new vulnerabilities in cancer. The process has been studied for decades, yet remains surprising.

stories.title: Experimental drug targets resistant leukemia
stories.summary: An experimental drug, PHI-101, has shown effectiveness against FLT3-positive acute myeloid leukemia in laboratory and animal studies. The drug aims to overcome genetic mutations that cause resistance to existing therapies. Researchers at Johns Hopkins are testing its potential to treat this aggressive subtype of the disease.

stories.title: Heart cells may use non-direct signaling
stories.summary: New evidence suggests heart cells transmit electrical signals through methods beyond direct connections. The heart beats at least 3 billion times over a human lifetime, maintaining its rhythm while the body sleeps, works, or exercises. The organ continues to function without requiring much thought from its owner.

stories.title: Brain immune cells linked to motor memory loss
stories.summary: Learning new movements changes the myelin insulating nerve fibers in the brain. A new study suggests that immune cells may weaken these motor memories by removing that insulation. The brain appears to be actively editing its own physical connections as it learns new skills.

stories.title: Tumor architecture impacts colorectal cancer treatment
stories.summary: Colorectal tumors exhibit high levels of heterogeneity, meaning cancer cells within a single patient display divergent behaviors. This diversity complicates treatment, as different cell states respond differently to therapy. Tumors are not uniform, which continues to reduce the overall efficacy of clinical interventions.

stories.title: Modified protein improves anticancer drug delivery
stories.summary: Researchers at Osaka Metropolitan University have modified a natural protein to hold anticancer drugs more securely. The goal is to prevent the medication from releasing prematurely before reaching the tumor site. The protein has been given a stronger grip on its cargo.

stories.title: ICMR survey reports decline in anaemia prevalence
stories.summary: The ICMR released findings from the 2023-2025 SAMPADA survey, showing a lower prevalence of anaemia across several age groups compared to previous data. The report provides national evidence on micronutrient deficiencies, noting an encouraging shift in health markers across the life course.

stories.title: ICMR survey finds high vitamin B12 deficiency in adolescents
stories.summary: A national survey by the ICMR found that approximately two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12. The study, conducted between 2023 and 2025, highlights concerns regarding long-term brain development and nerve function. The micronutrient is essential, yet currently absent in most of the surveyed population.

stories.title: India approves 19,983 health units under PM-ABHIM for emergency response - NewsBytes
Maharashtra reports 11 lakh free medical treatments
stories.summary: Over 11 lakh patients received free medical care in Maharashtra between January and November 2026 under two state and central health schemes. The programs provided 17 lakh treatments worth 2,869.45 crore rupees. Eligible families can access up to 5 lakh rupees in annual coverage.

stories.title: Government approves health infrastructure units
stories.summary: Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava has called for a mission-mode approach to strengthen public health infrastructure and emergency preparedness. The government approved 19,983 units under the PM-ABHIM initiative. Officials emphasized the need for better inter-departmental coordination and the use of digital health tools.

stories.title: Assam anaemia rates reported in ICMR survey
stories.summary: The ICMR survey indicates that over 70 percent of women and nearly half of men in Assam are anaemic. The data is part of the national SAMPADA report, which tracks markers of population health and nutrition across the country.

stories.title: India reports progress in tuberculosis incidence
stories.summary: India has reduced its tuberculosis incidence rate to 195 cases per 100,000 people in 2024, down from 237 in 2015. Despite this decline, the country still carries the largest global tuberculosis burden. It accounts for nearly one-quarter of all documented cases worldwide.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh reports high anaemia rates in elderly women
stories.summary: An ICMR-NIN survey found that 81.7 percent of women aged 60 and above in Andhra Pradesh are anaemic. This figure is significantly higher than the national average of 55.7 percent. The state also recorded the highest anaemia rates for children under five.

stories.title: Health Ministry flags substandard drug samples
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry reported that 324 drug samples failed quality tests in October 2026. State laboratories identified 287 of these batches, while central labs flagged 37. Authorities noted that these failures apply to the specific tested batches rather than all products under a brand name.

stories.title: Gaza health ministry reports 19 killed in 48 hours
stories.summary: Gaza’s health ministry reports 19 Palestinians were killed by Israeli attacks over the past 48 hours. The ministry states 74,772 people have been killed and 176,298 wounded since the war began on 7 October 2023. Total casualties since the October ceasefire are recorded at 1,705.

stories.title: Health Ministry : 44 Civilians killed & injured in Saudi enemy aggression over 48 hours - وكالة سبأ
Warraq fire kills 31 in Egypt
stories.summary: A fire caused by a petroleum truck crash on the Ring Road in Giza killed 31 people and injured 21. The Public Prosecution has opened an investigation into the incident, and the cabinet plans to review fuel transport regulations once the cause is established.

stories.title: Fighting in eastern Congo forces Ebola workers to evacuate, disrupts outbreak response - France 24
Cebu hospitals open dengue express lanes, no outbreak, says DOH - Cebu Daily News
Ebola outbreak in Congo surpasses 12,000 cases
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has reached 12,000 confirmed cases. Government data indicates that ongoing fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting containment efforts for the disease.

stories.title: Giza tunnel fire death toll reaches 30
stories.summary: A fire above the Ashara Tunnel in the Warraq district of Giza killed 30 people and injured 15. The Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population confirmed the casualties and stated that the injured have been transported to three local hospitals for medical treatment.

stories.title: Gastroenteritis outbreak at Waikato school camp
stories.summary: More than 400 people attended a school camp in Waikato where an outbreak of gastroenteritis has occurred. Students, parents and staff have reported vomiting and diarrhoea. Health officials note the illness has spread to household members of those who attended the event.

stories.title: Vehicle fire in Egypt kills 31
stories.summary: A vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on a major ring road in Cairo, killing 31 people and injuring 21. The incident occurred above a tunnel in the al-Warak neighbourhood of Giza. Local media reported the truck hit a central reservation before igniting.

stories.title: KNUST launches TekMed app for digital health
stories.summary: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology has launched the TekMed app. The university says the tool aims to transform healthcare delivery through digital innovation and artificial intelligence. The launch occurred during the university's second Research Week at the campus hospital.

stories.title: Africa CDC and PATH discuss AI health cooperation
stories.summary: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and the organization PATH held a meeting to discuss cooperation in artificial intelligence and digital health. The groups are exploring how emerging technologies could strengthen the capacity to detect and respond to future disease outbreaks across the continent.

stories.title: Report highlights Indian AI tools for health
stories.summary: A report from India Narrative suggests India's AI solutions could transform healthcare in developing economies. The report cites companies like Qure.ai and DeepTek for their radiology tools. A 2025 government-funded assessment found Qure.ai's technology to be clinically relevant for tuberculosis screening.

stories.title: Global Digital Health Forum 2026 to meet in Bangkok
stories.summary: The Global Digital Health Forum 2026 will be held in Bangkok from 2 to 4 December. The event aims to advance digital health and artificial intelligence in low and middle income countries. It will bring together government leaders, researchers and technology providers.

stories.title: Arogya Manthan 2026: J.P. Nadda highlights expansion of AB PM-JAY and digital health ecosystem - DD News
Remidio launches AI platform for systemic health screening
stories.summary: Remidio Innovative Solutions has released Systemic Health AI, a platform designed to screen retinal images for cardiovascular and chronic kidney disease indicators. The company says the technology allows clinics to assess heart, kidney and eye health during a single, non-invasive screening session.

stories.title: West Midlands to lead national NHS AI monitoring project - Home | Digital Health
Chennai surgeon performs robotic telesurgery
stories.summary: A surgeon in Chennai performed a robotic procedure on a patient 2,321 km away in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. The 45-minute surgery used the SSI Mantra system to remove uterine fibroids. The hospital described the event as a demonstration of remote surgical technology.

stories.title: IIT Bombay Wins Gold Medal For Excellence In Health Technology Research - شبكة تواصل الإخبارية
Mindfulness linked to healthier social media use
stories.summary: A review of 43 studies involving 28,000 participants suggests that mindfulness is associated with healthier social media habits and lower levels of depression, anxiety, and loneliness. Mindfulness is defined as observing thoughts without judgement. It appears that paying attention to one's own mind helps with the feed.

stories.title: Study finds weak links between creativity and mental health
stories.summary: A study of 14,600 twins published in Molecular Psychiatry found weak associations between artistic creativity and diagnoses including schizophrenia and anxiety disorders. The research analyzed data from the Swedish Twin Registry. The long-standing question of genius and madness remains largely a matter of statistical nuance.

stories.title: Creativity and mental health links remain complex
stories.summary: Researchers from the Max Planck Institute and Karolinska Institute found that while high levels of artistic creativity are associated with mental health problems, this correlation is largely absent for scientific creativity. The study in Molecular Psychiatry suggests the relationship between genius and madness is more complex than expected.

stories.title: Psilocybin users continue standard mental health care
stories.summary: A study published in Psychological Medicine found that people with depression who use psilocybin do not abandon conventional psychiatric services. They use telehealth and prescription medications at rates similar to non-users, while reporting higher levels of unmet needs. The psychedelic experience does not replace the appointment book.

stories.title: Study links caffeine consumption to adolescent brain changes
stories.summary: Research from King's College London involving 9,632 adolescents found that higher caffeine intake is linked to smaller brain surface area and increased mental health problems six months later. The study analyzed data from children aged 9 to 11. Adolescence is already a difficult time for the brain.

stories.title: Framework proposed to define art therapy
stories.summary: A study in Nature Mental Health proposes five mechanisms, including creative self-expression and symbolism, to distinguish professional art therapy from general wellness activities. Researchers note that the term is often used as an umbrella, making it difficult to evaluate clinical evidence. Art now requires a formal definition.

stories.title: Art therapy seeks clearer clinical distinction
stories.summary: A perspective piece in Nature Mental Health argues that the term art therapy is currently used as an umbrella, which complicates evidence synthesis and confuses practitioners. The authors propose a mechanism-informed scaffold to separate the regulated profession from broader social prescribing. Clarity is the new creative goal.

stories.title: Bath students turn to AI for mental health support
stories.summary: A study of 2,020 students at the University of Bath found that one in four used AI for mental health support, with usage rising among those feeling distressed. The survey had a low response rate of 9.1 percent. Students are increasingly asking algorithms for emotional guidance.

stories.title: Psychosocial interventions show promise for burn survivors
stories.summary: A scoping review indicates that targeted psychosocial therapies can alleviate depressive symptoms in burn survivors. However, the authors note that high risk of bias and small study cohorts currently prevent these interventions from becoming standardized clinical protocols. The path to a standard protocol remains under construction.

research.title: Common supplements rival antibiotics in treating severe gum disease
research.summary: A combination of omega-3 and low-dose aspirin produced results comparable to antibiotics when used alongside standard treatment for severe gum disease, with benefits persisting long after supplementation ended. The surprising discovery could offer an alternative for some patients while reducing reliance on antibiotics.

research.title: Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 26 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04754-3 Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analyses of wastewater and surveillance samples during the 2024−2025 measles outbreak in South Africa reveal previously undetected inter-provincial spread and transmission links, suggesting that wastewater-integrated whole-genome surveillance can improve measles monitoring and control efforts.

research.title: World’s largest trial of robotic knee replacement reveals surprising results
research.summary: Robot-assisted knee replacement surgery offers greater surgical precision, but a landmark clinical trial has revealed a surprising limitation. Despite the advanced technology, patients experienced no meaningful improvements in pain, mobility, or recovery compared with conventional surgery after one year.

research.title: Scientists discover a surprising twist in how the body burns calories
research.summary: Researchers have discovered that a drug can significantly increase the body's energy expenditure without clearly activating calorie-burning brown fat. The unexpected finding reveals a new challenge in developing obesity treatments that harness the body's natural fat-burning machinery.
